To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we propose a novel finite accurate FD scheme to improve the numerical accuracy of FD computations and to save hardware resources.

a new class of high-accuracy finite difference (FD) schemes was proposed; the FD coefficients of the new FD scheme can be represented with only few bits without deteriorating the numerical accuracy; the new FD scheme was efficiently implemented on FPGA using a hybrid floating-point/fixedpoint accumulator with group-alignment technology; the proposed RC-based FD computing engine can provide similar or even better accuracy than standard floating-point FD computing engines but consumes only a small fraction of hardware resources and can achieve higher computational performance.
we proposed an efficient implementation of finite difference computing engine on FPGAs, which is more compact and faster than previous works.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following three aspects: 1) the development of a new class of finite-accurate finite difference (FAD) schemes for high-accuracy computing; 2) the development of efficient floating-point arithmetic units and group alignment technology to implement high-accuracy FD computing engine; 3) the development of FPGA-based high-accuracy FD solver for transient physical phenomenon simulation.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the proposed finite-accurate finite-difference method with optimized FD coefficients and a new hybrid fixed-point/floating-point summation technique is a promising solution for the design of efficient FD computing engines on FPGA platforms.
the proposed FD computing engine with group-alignment hybrid accumulator is a very efficient and compact solution for high-accuracy FD computing on FPGAs.
our new design can be applied to any FD-based scientific and engineering simulations and result in a much more efficient implementation with much higher computational performance.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the new finite-accurate high-precision computing engine can achieve 2-4 times speedup and 2-5 times resource saving than standard IEEE-754 floating point arithmetic units.
we have successfully implemented a high-performance FD computing engine on FPGAs with finite-accurate coefficients.

we have developed an efficient RC-based FD computing engine with optimized finite-accuracy FD schemes and group-alignment floating-point accumulator for solving large-scale time-dependent PDEs on FPGA platforms.

the finite accurate FD coefficients can be represented in a few bits, and can provide similar numerical accuracy with much less hardware resources.
